messages:
lina_s (Sales): Hey team — Sierra (prospect) wants a perf POC next Tue. Main asks: variable burst patterns, sustained throughput target, and they attached a security questionnaire. Can eng + solutions scope a runbook and quick cost estimate?

raj_e (Eng): Yep. We need a few inputs first: expected avg QPS, typical prompt size (tokens in/out), and whether they need private/VPC deployment for the POC. Also: region preference and whether we should use Dedicated vs Hosted.

marta_solutions: From initial sec call: they want TLS + customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), VPC peering for control-plane, and audit logs for all inference requests. They said SOC2 evidence is required before pilot sign-off. Not sure if they demand Private for POC or can do Dedicated with peering.

lina_s (Sales): They said they'd prefer not to run on-prem for the POC but will accept Dedicated with VPC peering. Avg QPS target 400 sustained, with expected microbursts up to 2k for <30s. Typical prompt ~160 tokens in, ~120 tokens out. p95 latency target <= 250ms.

raj_e (Eng): Good. Proposed run plan (high-level):
- Warmup: 5m @ 50 QPS to populate caches
- Ramp: 10m linear ramp to 500 QPS
- Sustained: 30m @ 400-600 QPS (verify throughput)
- Microburst window: 3x bursts at 2k QPS for 30s separated by 10m
- Cooldown: 5m @ 50 QPS

Key metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, token/sec, KV cache hit rate, GPU util, queue length, error rate (429/5xx), and per-request token counts. We'll also run a tail-latency trace for a subset of requests.

raj_e (Eng): Load script example (vegeta) — we’ll do POSTs to Redwood API with the same payload shape they use.

```bash
echo '{"model":"rw-13b-v1","input":"<sample prompt>","max_tokens":120}' > body.json
vegeta attack -rate=400 -duration=30m -targets=<(printf "POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\n@body.json") | vegeta report
```

marta_solutions: For Dedicated with VPC peering we need: customer AWS account CIDR, peering window, and KMS key ARN. Security Q asks for HSM-backed CMKs — we can confirm we support customer-managed CMKs (bring-your-own) on the control plane and encryption at rest for artifacts.

kevin_oncall: FYI, if bursts hit 2k QPS we should enable autoscaling/burst capacity on the Dedicated pool. Also add a fallback policy to route to a cheaper model variant if latency spikes (canary rollouts). I'll add a runbook snippet for emergency throttling.

kevin_oncall: Quick runbook snippet:
```text
- If p95 > 500ms for >2m, disable bursts and shift 30% traffic to lower-cost model (rw-7b-quant).
- If errors >1% for 5m, abort POC and collect debug dump: /var/log/redwood/serving/*.log
```

lina_s (Sales): Pricing ask from Sierra: they want an estimate for a 2-week pilot with the above pattern + a monthly estimate at 400 QPS sustained. Any ballpark numbers we can give?

raj_e (Eng): Quick ballpark calc (very rough): assume avg tokens per request = 280 (in+out). At 400 QPS sustained -> 400 * 280 * 3600 * 24 * 30 = tokens/month. Easier: tokens/sec = 400 * 280 = 112k tokens/s -> ~9.6B tokens/day -> ~288B tokens/month. Oof. For 2-week pilot we'd do much less.

marta_solutions: For pricing we should translate to cost per 1M tokens. Sales: recommend we provide two scenarios — Hosted per-token pricing vs Dedicated reserved capacity estimate (monthly commit) — and call out burst overage charges.

raj_e (Eng): For the POC we can run a scaled-down synthetic that preserves shape (same burst ratios but 10% load) and extrapolate. That avoids massive costs while validating tail latencies. Recommend we propose a smoke run at full shape but 10% amplitude, then one full-run day to validate autoscaling and KV cache behavior.

lina_s (Sales): Agree. Sierra prefers real numbers though — will they accept extrapolated estimates? I'll flag with them.

marta_solutions: Action items: 
- Raj: draft the vegeta/wrk scripts and the metric dashboard (p95/p99, token/sec, cache-hit) by EOD tomorrow.
- Kevin: write the emergency throttling + fallback policy and make sure alerting hooks to their PagerDuty.
- Lina: get CIDR + KMS ARN + sample payload from Sierra. Also confirm they accept Dedicated with VPC peering for the POC.

raj_e (Eng): Will do. Also: small note on payload shaping — if they use streaming responses we need to instrument stream latencies separately; vegeta won't capture chunked streaming well. We might need a custom runner for streaming workloads.

lina_s (Sales): They do use streaming in one flow. Can we cover that in the pilot?

raj_e (Eng): Yes — we can run a separate streaming test using a simple parallel goroutine client that maintains N connections and measures first-byte, last-byte, and total time. Sample pseudocode I'll attach to the runbook.

marta_solutions: Security checklist for packet: VPC peering, KMS CMK ARN, SOC2 docs, penetration test report window, and contract addendum for audit logs. I'll draft a short note for legal review.

deploy-bot: deploy status: Dedicated pool blueprint "sierra-dedicated-1" provisioned in us-west-2 (eta ~45m).

raj_e (Eng): Nice. Once provisioned I'll kick off the scaled smoke test (10% amplitude). Will post initial results in this thread.

lina_s (Sales): Thanks everyone. If we can get the smoke numbers (tail latencies + GPU util) and a modeled cost estimate tomorrow we can present to Sierra on Thurs. :thumbsup:

kevin_oncall: One more: include a run with KV cache disabled to show worst-case cold-start latencies. That matters for their SLA questions.

raj_e (Eng): Good call. We'll include that as a short 5m test after warmup.

lina_s (Sales): Perfect — I'll update Sierra with the plan and collect the KMS/cidr/payload.

raj_e (Eng): Quick note: expected outputs from smoke run to paste in deck: p95, p99, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU util, cache hit%, and an extrapolated cost table (hosted vs dedicated).

marta_solutions: I'll start the security doc template now.

kevin_oncall: I'll also add alerting thresholds to the runbook (p95>300ms notify, errors>0.5% page).

raj_e (Eng): ETA: smoke run + initial numbers by 3123457320.

lina_s (Sales): Great — thanks team.
